content.title: Reproduce: regenerate returns 401 in open auth mode (BUG-1)
content.description: Reproduce BUG-1: POST /api/users/:name/regenerate returns 401 in open auth mode. Confirm the root cause — the webapp server route (packages/webapp/server/routes/users.ts:54) calls tracker.usersRegenerate(name) without forwarding auth context, so resolveAuthor returns the default user ('anonymous') which fails the self-service check in usersRegenerate (callerName !== targetName). Note: e2e/packages/webapp/e2e/phase4-validation.spec.ts:197-216 currently asserts this 401 (locking the bug in as passing).

content.content:
Done. BUG-1 reproduced and root cause confirmed.

**Reproduction:**
- Manual: POST to the regenerate endpoint in open auth mode returns HTTP 401 with code INVALID_TOKEN and message "You can only regenerate your own token."
- The existing E2E test e2e/phase4-validation.spec.ts:198 ("returns 401 in open mode without token — BUG-1") passes, confirming the bug is currently locked in.

**Root cause confirmed:**
packages/webapp/server/routes/users.ts:54 calls tracker.usersRegenerate(name) passing only the target user's name and forwarding no auth/caller context. Inside the tracker, resolveAuthor then returns the default author ("anonymous") in open auth mode, which fails the self-service check (callerName !== targetName) inside usersRegenerate, producing the 401.

**Server log captured during reproduction:**
- [Error] You can only regenerate your own token.
- --> POST regenerate endpoint 401 1ms

**Scope note for the fix:** The fix belongs to webapp-developer (forward the caller identity / token from the request to usersRegenerate). Once fixed, the Phase 4 test at lines 197-216 must be rewritten to assert a 200 + new token response instead of the 401.

No code changed — validation only.
